snapshot.statement:
A pharmaceutical distributor runs workloads in its own datacenter, in Azure, and in another public cloud. Management wants one consistent way to govern, inventory, and monitor all of these environments instead of using disconnected tools for each.

What is the purpose of Azure Arc?
options: To provide a browser-based shell for running interactive commands against Azure resources
To extend Azure management and governance to hybrid and multicloud resources through Azure Resource Manager
To assess on-premises virtual machines and then migrate them into Azure regions at scale
To define Azure infrastructure in declarative JSON files that make deployments repeatable and consistent
snapshot.referenceTitle: Azure Arc overview — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A grocery retailer will start using Azure Arc for the Windows and Linux servers in its regional datacenters. A junior engineer asks how those machines, which stay on-premises, become manageable with Azure tools.

How does Azure Arc make non-Azure resources manageable?
options: It projects existing non-Azure resources into Azure Resource Manager so they can be managed as if they ran in Azure
It replicates each on-premises server as a complete virtual machine in the nearest Azure region
It routes datacenter network traffic through an Azure VPN gateway so the servers appear to be inside Azure
It converts each server into an ARM template that can be redeployed inside an Azure subscription
snapshot.referenceTitle: Azure Arc overview — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A hospital network wants to keep several database and container workloads on-premises but manage them with Azure tools. The architecture team is checking which resource types Azure Arc can manage outside Azure.

Which set of resource types can Azure Arc manage outside Azure?
options: Azure Functions, Logic Apps, and Azure App Service instances
Azure Virtual Networks, subnets, and VPN gateways
Windows and Linux servers only; databases and Kubernetes clusters must run in Azure
Servers, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services, and SQL Server hosted outside Azure
snapshot.referenceTitle: Azure Arc overview — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A mining company must keep its warehouse management system on on-premises servers for three more years, but security leadership wants those servers to follow the same policies, inventory, and monitoring as the company's Azure resources, starting now.

Which approach should the company choose?
options: Use Azure Migrate to assess the servers and replicate them into an Azure region where the policies apply
Use ExpressRoute to create a private network connection, which will bring the connected servers under Azure Policy
Use Azure Arc to project the servers and apply the same policies, inventory, and monitoring as cloud resources
Replicate the servers' data to an Azure Storage account and apply Azure Policy to that storage account
snapshot.referenceTitle: Azure Arc overview — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A software vendor's engineering director wants infrastructure changes handled the way application code is: reviewed, versioned, and reproducible by anyone on the team. A junior developer asks what the practice is called.

Which statement describes infrastructure as code?
options: Recording the manual steps needed to configure each environment in a shared operations document
Defining and deploying infrastructure through descriptive, versioned models instead of configuring environments by hand
Backing up infrastructure settings after every change so they can be restored if an environment drifts
Monitoring resource utilization and letting automation resize resources as demand changes
snapshot.referenceTitle: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)? — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
At a food delivery platform, each test environment was configured manually by different engineers. The environments have drifted apart, deployments fail unpredictably, and nobody can reproduce them exactly. The engineering manager wants any team member to be able to rebuild an identical environment on demand.

Which practice addresses this problem?
options: Apply resource locks to the test environments so that no one can modify their settings
Have each engineer maintain a wiki page describing the changes they made to each environment
Follow Azure Advisor recommendations to bring the environments into alignment
Adopt infrastructure as code so that every environment is generated from the same versioned definition
snapshot.referenceTitle: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)? — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A game studio redeploys its staging infrastructure frequently. The lead engineer wants the assurance that applying the same deployment definition to an environment — whether it is empty, partially configured, or already complete — always converges to the same end state.

Which IaC principle provides this assurance?
options: Idempotence, where a given operation always produces the same result regardless of the environment's starting state
Declarative syntax, where the definition file lists the exact commands to execute, in order
Orchestration, where engineers sequence every resource creation step manually in the definition
Modularity, where every environment receives its own separate and uniquely maintained definition file
snapshot.referenceTitle: What is infrastructure as code (IaC)? — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
An e-commerce company provisions its Azure environment with a long Bash script: create the network, then the virtual machines, then the database, in a strict sequence. When a step fails mid-script, the environment is left half-built. The team wants to describe the desired end state once and let the platform determine the steps and deploy them in the correct order.

Which approach should the team adopt?
options: Rewrite the same step-by-step commands as an Azure PowerShell script with thorough error handling
Run the existing Bash script inside Azure Cloud Shell instead of on a local terminal
Define the environment in an ARM template declaring the resources, then deploy it through Resource Manager
Perform the steps manually in the Azure portal and record them in an operations runbook
snapshot.referenceTitle: What are ARM templates? — Microsoft Learn

snapshot.statement:
A nonprofit's IT team is studying how Azure handles resource operations behind the scenes. A volunteer with cloud experience asks for a plain definition of Azure Resource Manager.

Which statement describes Azure Resource Manager?
